correctness.rationale: For unweighted Bergman A²(D) with e_n=sqrt(n+1)z^n and the *monomial* decimator W z^(2n)=z^n (zero on odd powers), W e_2n=sqrt((2n+1)/(n+1))e_n; its compact asymptote is sqrt(2)J where J is normalized even-index decimation. Symbols continuous and zero on the circle yield compact Toeplitz operators by uniform cutoff and compact interior Bergman inclusion. For each boundary Fourier mode z^k or conjugate z^k, the Bergman Toeplitz matrix differs compactly from unilateral shift S^k or S*^k, reducing to sqrt(2)J L_p modulo compacts. Even/odd coefficient splitting gives a row of two unilateral Laurent Toeplitz blocks with symbols a(zeta)=sum_r c_(2r)zeta^r, b(zeta)=sum_r c_(2r+1)zeta^(r+1); the row Calkin norm equals sup_zeta sqrt(|a|²+|b|²), by bilateral compression upper bound and weakly-null long plane-wave packets lower bound. The antipodal parallelogram identity yields ||B_phi||_e=max_{|eta|=1}sqrt(|phi(eta)|²+|phi(-eta)|²). Trigonometric approximation and Poisson extension extend to all continuous closed-disk symbols; compact iff boundary values vanish. Independent monomial/polyphase identities and unit-circle grid tests give 2 for 1+z and 2sqrt(2) for 1+z², plus 101 antipodal Fourier checks, but finite data alone do not establish the Calkin formula.
